findings.title: Named-control capture replay does not retain the original modifier chord
findings.qualification: Authenticated executable Windows source only; no AHK or native input/editor ran. The conditional reproduction requires a genuine configured named-control completion. Native suppression/pass-through and final receiving are explicitly unmeasured; no duplicate delivery is claimed.
findings.reproduction: Use a blank scratch editor, CapsWord/hotstrings/Enter remaps off, and arm one_shot_shift via an independent configured action. After arming hold LCtrl (independently Shift) and press Enter within the2s timeout, retaining the modifier during replay. Conditional on the explicit native named-control completion, the producer requests SendNewResult("{Enter}",False,False) with no original modifier attribution. Its default non-atomic nonliteral path uses ordinary SendEvent, which the existing tap sender contract documents as lifting external modifiers. The request is bare Enter rather than the captured Ctrl/Shift+Enter. Test Ctrl+Backspace/Delete similarly. This is source-derived, not a native event trace.
findings.root_cause: _SIHO_ReadScalar publishes a named control without its completing modifier chord. OneShotShift replays only Capture.Name via normal SendNewResult/SendEvent, unlike the guarded tap-key producer which explicitly retains modifiers. DeadKey uses the same decoder and ordinary Send for its sibling control branch.
findings.silent_failure: The control name and plain-key send are individually accepted; no diagnostic detects lost chord identity. Existing end-key meta checks pin the named list/order, while native scalar fixtures require physical modifiers released and settlement/rearm probes assert unmodified controls or emitter calls.
findings.regression_test: Execute actual capture and public replay for unmodified and Ctrl/Shift/Alt/Win-modified Backspace/Enter/Delete; retain the completing modifier identity and final destination/admission through Wait and output. Include modifier release between capture and replay, pause/rearm and native refusal, exactly-once receiving and sibling DeadKey controls. Adding Blind alone preserves current modifiers, which may differ from the original capture. Genuine AHK/native application execution is still needed.

findings.title: Caps Lock plus held Shift loses requested one-shot title
findings.qualification: Actual public Keymap callback and original adapter/state/policy with original parser of shipped layout. Translation, clock, events and collector are recording ports; no Quartz, native CapsWord activation or receiving-application proof.
findings.reproduction: With Caps Lock and physical Shift held, arm one-shot and send keycode 0. The shipped first-four-map projection translates to a; shared policy requests A; callback retains flags 196608 and spends the deadline without replacement. Matched no-modifier, Caps-only and Shift-only controls produce A.
findings.root_cause: Adapter validates Shift alone against the requested title, then ORs Shift into original flags already containing Caps Lock and Shift. The actual prospective flag combination still translates to lowercase.
findings.silent_failure: Activation is spent and the callback returns an accepted unchanged event without diagnosing that the requested title was not produced. Actual application receipt is unmeasured.
findings.regression_test: Run original public callback with Caps Lock and either held Shift, verify translation under complete prospective flags equals the requested title or choose serialized title output. Preserve physical flags and matching release ownership; add native application receiving separately.

findings.title: Programmatic timeout validation publishes values rejected by arming
findings.qualification: Actual Remap setter/transaction with acknowledged persistence port and actual public Keymap arm executed separately, linked by real getter/setter contract. No actual disk, ordinary-menu failure, simultaneous full-app instance or native application failure. Supplemental setter still uses acknowledged persistence/no-op logger ports; actual shared formatter is independently executed over a recorded sink. No full real Config persistence or native logger transport is claimed.
findings.reproduction: Call public Remap.set_sticky_timeout with 0.1 or 0.9 milliseconds while remapping is disabled in the registered transaction fixture. The real setter accepts, publishes getter zero and sends zero to acknowledged save port. Separately original Keymap.arm_one_shot_shift with that getter value raises invalid one-shot Shift timeout. Controls include 0, 1, 2.5 and 2000; the ordinary menu floors first and rejects zero. Supplement: original setter with numeric NaN returns true and publishes NaN through live getter/acknowledged save payload; independent original public arm with NaN raises invalid one-shot Shift timeout. Positive infinity is accepted by both owners and stays active at recorded clock1e12; this is characterization, not proof of a supported unlimited menu choice.
findings.root_cause: Setter tests positivity before flooring, allowing a positive fraction to become zero after validation; public arming requires strictly positive timeout. The value <= 0 guard also admits numeric NaN, which the arm timeout > 0 contract rejects.
findings.silent_failure: Transaction reports accepted mutation and acknowledged zero save payload despite the published value violating the arm precondition; arming raises explicitly rather than silently succeeding.
findings.regression_test: Validate after flooring or require integer milliseconds before mutation, assert rejected fractions preserve live and persistence values, and run actual setter/getter-to-arm contract plus loaded configuration validation. Keep ordinary menu rejection as control. Include numeric NaN, numeric strings, finite values around one, both infinities and transaction refusals; define infinity policy explicitly.

findings.title: Ordinary one-shot wrapped-letter repeat unexpectedly retires the keyboard channel
additional_properties: matching original output ownership for repeat
findings.qualification: Loud fail-safe; no native stuck-key/app receipt; physical standalone tap route, not unsupported legacy logical-pair admission. Original owners over explicitly recording native ports; this role does not execute native inverse generation or native receiving. The supplementary transport constructs an unused legacy owner/base before actual Manager replacement; no declaration override, unavailable fixture load or generic action occurs during events. Reachability concerns the enabled shipped preset, not neutral defaults.
findings.reproduction: Quick-tap default physical RightCtrl; press A; send legitimate EV_KEY repeat value 2 before release through original Reader/Hook/broker/Writer. Broker refuses code30/value2; Hook inactive, debt and output/source retirement are observed before teardown. No-repeat control remains active and produces Aa. Additional original-channel control uses unchanged production declarations, empty valid config.toml and explicitly enabled shipped preset; both runtimes still reproduce repeat retirement and healthy Aa without repeat.
findings.root_cause: wrapped EV_KEY repeat gets holder identity only if input_arms[self], absent on ordinary physical tap arming
findings.silent_failure: Failure is loud: emergency raw ownership settlement refusal retires the input channel. No native stuck-key or receiving-app outcome is established.
findings.regression_test: Drive ordinary physical tap, repeat and release through original broker and Writer lifetime; retain original output holder and active session. Preserve guarded logical-arm, refusal and no-repeat controls.

capabilities.basis: Actual shared Lua policy/Unicode and actual macOS state owner, or actual declaration/model guard where named. AHK relationships are source-only. No native event adapter, keyboard or receiving application is certified.

capabilities.windows: Snapshot before InputHook waiting
capabilities.macos: Live magic reader on event
capabilities.linux: Live magic reader on event
capabilities.basis: Shared J result explicit; setting lifetime differs. Current allowed magic symbols do not collide with ASCII table keys. Actual config changes during a pending capture are not certified.

capabilities.contract: An action origin is not a whole capability
capabilities.windows: Generic catalogue and tap action available
capabilities.macos: sticky_shift explicit generic equivalent and native tap source
capabilities.linux: Reserved tap one_shot_shift exists; generic catalogue names absent
capabilities.basis: Exact catalogue/platform projection and separate reserved tap namespace; OS accessibility Sticky Keys is not assumed to reproduce Ergopti special punctuation mappings.

capabilities.windows: right_ctrl
capabilities.macos: right_option
capabilities.linux: right_ctrl
capabilities.basis: Shared defaults and explicit namespace reconciliation table document these differences; physical admission remains per-driver.

capabilities.contract: Default and editable deadline
capabilities.windows: Shared2000ms; nonpositive constant falls back2s
capabilities.macos: Same default; positive sticky_timeout_ms user override through hs-only menu
capabilities.linux: Shared2000ms registry value
capabilities.basis: Shared timing registry and explicit per-driver menu construction. No common permanent exclusion policy is inferred from missing controls.

capabilities.contract: User-facing zero or unlimited timeout setting
capabilities.windows: Nonpositive constant fallback2s
capabilities.macos: No unlimited UI preset established; ordinary menu rejects zero. Original state Owner.arm separately accepts positive infinity; fractional setter can publish rejected zero (OSM-002).
capabilities.linux: No same user setting; registry default positive
capabilities.basis: No supported zero/unlimited UI choice established. A separate original state-owner probe accepts math.huge: positive does not imply finite. It does not execute the setter with infinity or establish persistence support. Historical TODO wording is not current feature evidence.

capabilities.macos: Actual shared/state controls cover5 names
capabilities.linux: Shared policy covers5; native producer classification driver-owned
capabilities.basis: Actual shared Lua policy/Unicode and actual macOS state owner, or actual declaration/model guard where named. AHK relationships are source-only. No native event adapter, keyboard or receiving application is certified.

capabilities.linux: Actual shared Unicode title includes expansions

capabilities.contract: A second activation has precise ownership

capabilities.macos: Internal owner refreshes deadline and preserves old key release debt
capabilities.linux: Native input-arm lease can refuse rearm while consumed
capabilities.basis: State/source mechanisms only; reaching them through a held trigger or another consumer may change admission.

capabilities.macos: Resolver predicate and adapter native flags are different layers
capabilities.linux: Resolver predicate and Hook/uinput lease are different layers
capabilities.basis: Actual shared resolver contracts tested, not all public native modifiers/CapsWord combinations; peers own concrete driver findings.

capabilities.contract: One scalar is not an arbitrary event payload
capabilities.windows: Complete scalar capture; multi-scalar native receiving unexecuted
capabilities.macos: Actual state can title whole text; NNBSP% not scalar% special
capabilities.linux: Shared resolve takes text produced by key layout
capabilities.basis: Actual shared Lua policy/Unicode and actual macOS state owner, or actual declaration/model guard where named. AHK relationships are source-only. No native event adapter, keyboard or receiving application is certified.

capabilities.contract: Catalogue failures are explicit
capabilities.windows: Loud one-time empty-map degradation until restart
capabilities.macos: Construction refuses unreadable/malformed input
capabilities.linux: Read/parse refuses manager candidate
capabilities.basis: Source fault contracts only, no full startup/device receiving claim. Shipped valid data and baseline guard pass.

capabilities.contract: Preserve completing control chord identity
capabilities.windows: Named Backspace/Enter/Delete replay loses original modifier attribution; actual native admission and receiving unmeasured.
capabilities.macos: Controls spend through original callback; Cmd shortcuts retain activation. Modified control receiving is not fully certified.
capabilities.linux: Ctrl+Enter spends before shortcut lookup; Ctrl+A retains. Original ports only.
capabilities.basis: Conditional Windows source root; do not infer duplicate delivery or treat a named-control producer as native receiving.

capabilities.contract: First title under CapsLock and held Shift
capabilities.windows: Captured scalar/title send route; equivalent native receiving combination unexecuted.
capabilities.macos: Original callback spends title A but retains lowercase a under shipped-layout translation port.
capabilities.linux: Original public owners emit aB; inverse plan ignores live CapsLock; both Shift sides covered.
capabilities.basis: Two OS-scoped roots share a live-state planning limitation; recording ports qualify both; no physical application proof.

capabilities.contract: Keep first-key repeats and input channel ownership
capabilities.windows: Scalar capture and retirement source checked; native repeat receiving unexecuted.
capabilities.macos: Original callback repeat/release gives AAa; fresh overlapping keys give Abc.
capabilities.linux: Ordinary physical tap first-letter repeat is refused by original broker and retires channel; no-repeat control healthy.
capabilities.basis: Linux Reader/Hook/broker/Writer retirement is observed before teardown; no real evdev/uinput or native stuck-key claim. Additional enabled-shipped-preset control retains actual production declarations and empty valid config.toml; Lua5.4/LuaJIT reproduce the same failure without an unavailable declaration override.

capabilities.contract: Accepted timeout belongs to the arming numeric domain
capabilities.windows: Fixed shared constant with finite fallback; no matching public fractional setting.
capabilities.macos: Setter publishes zero from positive fractions, or numeric NaN, through acknowledged save port; separate public arm rejects both. Infinity accepted by setter and arm; no supported unlimited UI choice established.
capabilities.linux: Shared timing value; no same end-user fractional timeout setting.
capabilities.basis: Same numeric validation root (OSM-002); independently executed actual setter and public arm, declared persistence/lifecycle ports; original shared formatter handles nonfinite values via protected fallback. No ordinary UI or real-disk failure is claimed.

capabilities.contract: Shortcut and nonspending controls retain activation
capabilities.windows: Tab/Escape representation and modified native receiving not measured.
capabilities.macos: Cmd shortcut retains; Backspace/Enter/Tab/Escape spend; arrows/function keys retain in original callbacks.
capabilities.linux: Ctrl+A retains; Ctrl+Enter and five editing controls spend; arrows retain.
capabilities.basis: Control classification precedes shortcut lookup; no proven Mac/Linux Ctrl-control divergence and no claim of complete native control parity.

capabilities.contract: Pause, stop and stale ownership retire activation safely
capabilities.windows: Exact-token settlement, failed-cleanup owner retention and suspend guards checked from source only.
capabilities.macos: Pause disarms/refuses, resume remains plain; complete stop/outage reset owner; disarm preserves release debt intentionally.
capabilities.linux: Ordinary original-channel pause/resume/reload/stop clear arm; reload replaces Engine; guarded stale/partial ACK cases are separate owner invariants.
capabilities.basis: Mechanisms differ by ownership model. Source/declared-port checks do not certify native scheduling, receiving or cost.

capabilities.contract: Generated output informs adjacent CapsWord owner
capabilities.windows: OneShotShift itself does not cancel CapsWord; nearby cancellation belongs to ToggleCapsLock.
capabilities.macos: Direct punctuation serializer call lacks explicit CapsWord relay; combined serializer/watcher and native ordering unresolved.
capabilities.linux: Physical CapsLock cases characterize downstream lock; actual CapsWord activation plus one-shot receiving not executed.
capabilities.basis: Unresolved cross-owner candidate, excluded from confirmed finding count; no common automatic cancellation contract is invented.

capabilities.contract: Physical trigger paths retain OS-specific semantics
capabilities.windows: LAlt producer captures immediately then bounded Shift hold; RCtrl distinguishes tap and long Shift hold.
capabilities.macos: Recommended right Option plus sentinel/control route; sticky_shift calls dedicated Keymap arm, compound sticky actions use a separate owner.
capabilities.linux: RightCtrl standalone tap arms one-shot; canonical key-combination declarations reject one_shot_shift, independent of implemented physical tap route.
capabilities.basis: Documented platform/default namespaces and distinct producer source contracts; generic-action exclusion does not remove tap-hold implementation.
